title: Twenty WASP-105 b transit times lack sensitivity to tested circular inner planets of 1 to 25 Earth masses
abstract: We test whether the transit times of WASP-105 b can test the reported 2.0028-day inner candidate. Twenty complete TESS events from 2018 to 2026 agree with a linear ephemeris, with chi-square 13.95 for 18 degrees of freedom and a median timing error of 55.59 seconds. SAP photometry gives a similar result. Three circular, coplanar Newtonian models use inner masses of 1, 5 and 25 Earth masses. Input periods and phases are adjusted to match the reported mean transit ephemerides. The giant timing signal is about 0.10 second RMS per Earth mass; a five Earth-mass state gives about 18.55 seconds RMS for the inner candidate. The giant signals are below the measured error scale. An ideal five-sigma timing test of a five Earth-mass planet with 100 giant transits needs about one-second errors per event. This is a negative sensitivity result, not a mass bound or planet confirmation. Free eccentricity, other orbit states and transit-shape errors are not covered. Code, fitted event statistics, model event sequences, source hashes and a separate-scratch retrieval recipe permit reproduction.

display.caption: Measured giant transit timing errors exceed the circular common-host model signals. Lower panels show the candidate signal and ideal observing precision.
